author: ROME | Saint-JustPirate Y'aaar
content: Solana is getting significantly faster and fees are dropping.   But I don't think fees are at the heart of the issue.  Gameplay loops for small players is the real issue.  Assume that subsidizing small players and/or building an L2 is out of the question.  The only thing left to do is pay smaller players more.  But the problem with the current simplified loop is that if you pay smaller players more, the larger players will simply move to those loops and close out the smaller players.  Therefore we need loops that simply cannot be used in mass and/or by large players.   UE5 racing is the biggest example.  As a whale I can only race one ship at one time.  This puts me on even footing with smaller players.   If ATMTA wanted to pay small players $50 bucks a day in rewards, that would also be the max I could get it.  And it would be huge.     tl;dr bigger chunkier gameplay loops will increase rewards for small players

author: Oroboro [STAR]
content: I share the sentiments about the 2D game, especially considering we started with Escape Velocity and have built so much since then. We certainly share the team's opinion that SAGE in 2D should not be further developed, and instead, capacity should be redirected into Fleet Command, uniting all gameplay into UE5, which seems to meet current public demand. Not long ago, UE5 was called the cinematic walking simulator. I believe SAGE was a good start for getting the blockchain operations and economics right. Still, we realize day by day that limitations in balancing are present. There are lots of good ideas here, and I personally would wish that whales, especially the mentioned ones, would do more for the community and start using part of their LP earnings to actively develop tools for the community, as done by SLY, Eveeye, AEP Flipside, Superphoenix DAO, and many more. This is the only way, from my point of view, for the broader community to pull in the same direction, which is necessary for the team to develop and roll out more frequently. For the TH, I was expecting something more while I understand the message from Swager and the team on the Crew Packs. It needs to be something bigger. I would have expected something that would benefit the playstyle. I know the team just came out of the worst situation possible, but keeping people onboard requires something new and playable to experience. Again, I believe being a web3 whale comes with some sort of responsibility, unlike in real life, otherwise, people might not stay for long.

author: MightyNightmare [FRNT]
content:
This is the correct definition from the TH. As per my understanding, once parity is secured and the current web 2 solution is fully integrated into UE, the web 2-based browser game will be deprecated over time, considering that everybody will be able to play from any device (quote). Additionally, game mechanics might change in UE depending on what can be implemented one-to-one from web 2 into UE to achieve parity. It might be that some current game mechanics, as they are used at the moment, will not be present or will be different in the game we will play in the future. This is my take on the WIP of Project Galia at this point.

I just hope that the UE version will restrict multi-accounting to enhance a stronger faction association and build a faction-based community where players build their Empire based on economics and common targets, rather than players who believe gameplay is about filling gaps in LP distribution. There need to be differences and unequal development to drive factors such as faction diplomacy, trades, taxes, treaties, and conflicts. If all the faction economics are the same because the "gap" was leveled, players will focus on how to maximize LP across the faction, invalidating the decisions many players made in 2021 when they joined SA.

author: MightyNightmare [FRNT]
content:
Personally, I feel Oni is already engaging in this kind of gameplay under the leadership of ROME. It’s amazing to see their teamwork and achievements toward their faction. MUD is dominated by a Ustur account that is "currently" not interested in the development of the faction and faction strategy, rather than balancing the LP and Atlas emissions in one account. This would be necessary for small and medium players to develop and level up their accounts and invest more into game assets. This is not working at the moment as the LP is diluted, and the MUD player base will remain the same or decrease. This might turn into frustration, but I understand that the current game design and possibilities can't restrict multi-accounting, which is widely not accepted in many games and usually results in the exclusion of those accounts, including the freezing of those assets in a worst-case scenario.

There is no issue to be a member of a Multifaction Guild as you can still apply your gameplay towards a single faction.

author: MightyNightmare [FRNT]
content:
As an example related to my account as a medium player in MUD LP, I am within the top 10% of accounts. Running the rig 24/7 with a fully optimized setup, achieving over 90% efficiency, and timing all game loops with micromanagement while using SLY to operate transactions puts you in a position to reinvest in about 1-2 X5 or about 4 Airbikes per week. These earnings do not consider the SOL transaction fees, electricity costs, or time invested. This strategy works quite well with an LP around 15-20b and is motivating. If you reach about 25-30b, you will operate at cost.

There isn’t much more you can do to improve this situation. If LP remains at this level, you either quit or decide to enjoy the game in a pay-to-play style, as there is no chance to reinvest and counter the depreciating value of Atlas. If you consider the remaining players from the top 10% down to the tail end, you will see that those players are literally cut off. This needs to be addressed, and the best way is to let the "gaps" exist and see how they will be filled. The arbitrage only benefits the top 3% of players in my opinion. Certainly, they hold the biggest bags as well.

I would love to hear how ONI is managing this with their whales, but it seems to be working out for them.

author: SW4GN3R [STAR]
content: Not to sound cynical, but honestly, it's pre-alpha early access. It does come with the territory. And the game isn't funded. It's partially funded. And we're delivering product with that funding at the most reasonable pace we can. We're always faced with the trade off of polishing (with longer timelines) vs. releasing. And we're constantly getting pressure for updates. So that is a thread we try to carefully weave. People will be upset with any choice we make, regardless. What's most important to me at these early stages is getting the functional economy out, which is essentially the same as compensating our players for engaging now. And I'd argue we've done a pretty good job at that, and delivered a minimally entertaining product to start with. But we're also starting to reposition some of our focus on those more traditional gaming experiences, which are all of the features we described in the Town Hall. Bottom line, anyone engaging today should be aware of that early-access dynamic of buggy experiences. Perhaps we just need to do a better job explaining that to people.

And we're constantly getting pressure for updates. So that is a thread we try to carefully weave. People will be upset with any choice we make, regardless. What's most important to me at these early stages is getting the functional economy out, which is essentially the same as compensating our players for engaging now. And I'd argue we've done a pretty good job at that, and delivered a minimally entertaining product to start with. But we're also starting to reposition some of our focus on those more traditional gaming experiences, which are all of the features we described in the Town Hall. Bottom line, anyone engaging today should be aware of that early-access dynamic of buggy experiences. Perhaps we just need to do a better job explaining that to people.

But a piece of advice: if you want to keep complaining, it would be advisable for you to get informed about the situation (not only in SA but for Solana as well) and how it is changing, because people get tired of answering the same questions over and over again.

Honestly the mixed gameplay approach Star Atlas is building towards is much more fun and practical to draw in more players when time is scarce for players who have families or busy lives. More mining, exploring, player collisions that could create space battles, PVP fighting, lore, PVE, large player instances, and less time waiting while flying sounds better to me. Or if we are waiting while flying we can zoom out and manage a larger fleets. Ah can't wait.  Should I start posting videos to remind players why UE5 is going to put Star Atlas in a different league of development once the foundation is laid?

author: [SAI] Sim [STAR]
content:
Guys, I have a confession to make: I have never tried to understand or delve into the SDUs. I mean, I've read a bit, but I've never tried to understand the algorithm behind them scientifically.

Clearly, these are secrets that people tend to keep to themselves, understandably, but just for the sake of discussion: why do people only scan in the center of Galia? I've tried to explain it to myself in every possible way: maybe the probability increases with the distance from the SB? Maybe the center of Galia simply has a higher density of SDUs? (Not in terms of quantity, but perhaps sectors "recharge" more quickly?)

But the fundamental question is: are we sure that the generation and distribution algorithm of SDUs favors those in the center? Obviously, this is in addition to the "problem" of player competition.

Thanks

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content:
@bunthius Yes the sheet that was put together was a huge help that explained all the crew perks and what they did. There are still some things that are very vague on the descriptions. For example does the social cohesion perk effect crafting efficiency? or just on ship tasks? Leadership: does that apply to crafting crew as well as crew on a ship does this effect combat or just crafting/research on a ship or scanning etc? What does performance tuning effect that is a ship system? Bombing reloads? or just shield regen, repair, drone operation, rig operation etc.? Again there is more stuff these are just examples.

Sorry if my question was a bit vague I apologize. I'm super excited for how complex everything is and normally I would just test this out in the game but we have no place to do this. Ships useage/performance especially between the fighters and different ship professions etc are a bit cloudy from my perspective to see how they will be balanced and interact with one another. Adding crew into that with such a huge impact on ship performance and utility etc. and again having to buy them before we actually know what we want to buy is very tough sell to myself right now lol. Sorry for the long follow up but this all kind of falls into product clarity for consumers. If we are pushing a lot more marketing buyers will want to know what they are buying. Was hoping for more clarity on these items and I'm sure not everyone feels as I do but I don't think I'm the only one that feels this way.
